Paper · 28 Jun 2025

High-yield polymerisation of cyclic nucleotides under wet-dry cycling

Caimi, Langlais, Fontana, Wunnava, Bellini, Braun, Fraccia · ACS Central Science 11:1546-1557

In a sentence

Repeated drying and wetting joins all four RNA letters into short chains, with no added activating chemicals.

In plain words

Warm-pond theories say pools that dry by day and refill by night could join RNA letters into chains. Here, nucleotides in a ring-shaped form joined up on their own when only water was added each cycle, at room temperature and mildly alkaline pH. The chains were short: a few percent reached four letters and about one in a thousand reached ten.

Technical detail

2',3'-cyclic nucleotides of A, U, G and C oligomerise without external activators under wet-dry cycling. Yields reach about 70% for G and at least 20% for the others; at pH 11 polymerisation is near-balanced across the four bases with Y = 36%. Products include up to 6% 4-mers and 0.1% 10-mers; growth and hydrolysis balance after about 10 cycles.

What we take from it

Planned test

First entry for the warm-pond row. The pond step table records that wet-dry cycling gives short mixed oligomers; the gap to copyable lengths is named.

Source checked against its DOI. Read the original.
